title: The covariate value at which the better treatment changes is often not estimable as a point, and borrowed precision can make its interval wrong
question: Is the covariate boundary between two treatments' optimality well enough determined at achievable interaction precision to report as a point, and do standard intervals for it hold when interaction information comes partly from between-trial variation?
design: One individual-data trial plus five aggregate trials; interaction 0.3, 0.15 or 0.05, two boundary positions, an ecological term absent or present; within-trial and combined estimators; delta-method and Fieller intervals, regret and the pointwise optimality map. 12 cells, 2000 replicates each.
answer: No. From one trial of 400 patients at a moderate interaction the exact (Fieller) 95% confidence set for the boundary was unbounded in 66% to 69% of replicates, while the delta-method interval was always finite and covered as little as 0.86 at the weakest interaction. Borrowing interaction precision from aggregate trials at different covariate means (81% of the precision) made the sets bounded, but a between-trial ecological term of 0.1 cut their coverage to 0.68 to 0.70 for a boundary away from the trials' mean covariate value. Treating by the point estimate at the moderate interaction lost 31% to 95% of the value of individualized treatment with one trial.
findings: Fieller sets bounded from one trial: 84% to 85% at interaction 0.3, 31% to 34% at 0.15, 7% to 9% at 0.05.
The pointwise probability that A is better, thresholded at 0.5, is the plug-in rule; its (0.025, 0.975) region is the Fieller set, so it changes the report, not the decision.
With the ecological term, combined-estimator coverage 0.68 to 0.70 at boundary 1.5 and 0.92 to 0.93 at 0.5; individual-trial coverage 0.95.
At interaction 0.05, treating by the estimated boundary did worse than treating everyone with the better treatment on average (regret share up to 3.6).
not_answered: Two treatments and one modifier; no modifier selection; closed-form frequentist estimators rather than ML-NMR; declared linear ecological term. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: The boundary x* = -delta/beta between two treatments' optimality, and regret of treating by its estimate
n_sim: 2000 per cell, 12 cells, two estimators each
